title: The Thermostat War Is Finally Over
trend: Instagram Reels 'War Is Over' (announce a small personal win with relief over a holiday track; New Engen Instagram list updated Nov 6 2026, US) + heating season / first cold November nights — roommates Bea and Hector fight a twelve-day thermostat war, the thermostat begs for peace, they sign a treaty at sixty eight and celebrate; twist: it is still freezing because the cat has opened the window every night since September to chat with a pigeon, so they have been heating the whole street
youtube_title: Day twelve of the roommate thermostat war... it's finally over ❄️
description:
Bea wants it warm. Hector wants it at sixty four for character building. The thermostat is tired of being touched, and the cat knows something nobody else does.

lines.text: Day twelve of the thermostat war. I can see my breath.
Sixty four degrees. It builds character.
You are wearing shorts, Hector. In November.
I am from a cold family. We run warm.
Your family is from Arizona.
I am the thermostat. Please stop touching me.
Today I was seventy one, then sixty four, then seventy one. I am dizzy.
He turns it down every time I leave the room.
She turns it up every time I blink.
I have been pressed more than an elevator button.
Why is the thermostat in your room, anyway?
The lease says whoever has the thermostat has the power.
The lease does not say that. That is pencil.
Pencil is a legal font.
I am wearing three coats. I made soup to hold it.
Last night she put a hair dryer on me. I thought it was summer.
And I put an ice pack on him. He thought it was Canada.
Two countries this week. I never left the wall.
Please. I am begging. Can we have peace talks?
Fine. Peace talks. Sit down, Hector.
My opening offer is sixty four. A strong number.
Seventy four. I want to wear a T shirt indoors.
What about sixty eight? Everyone is a little sad.
Deal. If I get the last pizza slice on Fridays.
Sixty eight. And you wear pants in the kitchen.
That is a big ask. Fine. Deal.
Please sign here. On my little screen. With your finger.
It is over. The war is over. We won.
Who won?
Everybody. That is how peace works.
Sixty eight. I am finally still. I could cry warm air.
Okay. We wait. Any minute now it gets cozy.
It has been one hour. Why is it still cold?
My soup has a skin on it.
Oh. You two noticed the cold. That is new.
Noodle? Why is there a breeze behind the cat?
The window. I open it every night. Since September.
You can open windows?
I have thumbs when nobody is looking.
Why would you open the window in November?
To talk to Gerald. He is a pigeon. He loves bread.
So for two months I have been heating the whole street.
Missus Patel downstairs grows tomatoes now. In November.
We fought for twelve days. And the cat was the enemy.
I am not your enemy. I am a neutral country.
Close the window. Close it right now.
Fine. Gerald will understand. Gerald always understands.
Oh my. Real sixty eight. It is beautiful.
I can feel my nose, Hector!
I am wearing pants. And I am happy.
We could have done this in October.
We needed to grow as people.
Gerald has a cousin. She is coming over.
Noodle. No birds in the apartment.
She is not a bird. She is a guest. Who is a bird.
Where is she going to sit?
On the thermostat. She heard it is warm.
Day one of the pigeon war.
